newsitem.title: USA: Former Gruntal executive pleads guilty to fraud.
newsitem.headline: Former Gruntal executive pleads guilty to fraud.

text.p: The former second-highest ranking officer at Gruntal & Co. has pleaded guilty to one count of making fraudulent and misleading entries in the broker's books and records, prosecutors said Thursday.
Edward Bao, formerly executive vice president of administration, faces up to 10 years in prison and a fine of $1 million. He pleaded guilty on Tuesday in federal court in Manhattan.
The entries were made in connection with a 10-year scheme to convert property belonging to Gruntal's customers, vendors and other broker-dealers to Gruntal's benefit, the U.S. Attorney's office said.

The converted property included dividends owed to customers and other broker-dealers; funds allotted to pay certain customers and vendors for checks that remained uncashed; property contained in dormant customer accounts and abandoned property owed to various states.
Bao is the third defendant who has pleaded guilty to charges arising from the scheme.
